page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge is a shared-core instance belonging to the burstable t5 family, deployed via KVM virtualization on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512f, and BMI2. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear distinction between parallel execution and single-thread throughput. Multi-core performance metrics fall within the middle tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7405.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 8206.2. In contrast, single-thread testing demonstrates lower output, with Geekbench single-core registering 775.0 and stress-ng single-core scoring 1038.97. High-memory throughput holds steady for small cached read blocks at 484.8 GB/sec, but drops to 53.95 GB/sec for uncached large reads. Application testing shows strong Redis SET handling at 7.37 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures at 4.33 GB/sec and small-model LLM generation reaches 67.31 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge centers on its burstable CPU allocation and lack of onboard storage. Because vCPU capacity is governed by a burstable allocation profile, sustained high-load workloads risk CPU throttling once execution credits deplete. In terms of resource density, it delivers an economical balance of compute cores to memory for intermittent tasks. The instance is suited for non-production environments, code compilation and build servers, background worker queues, staging deployments, and batch processing workloads that experience variable CPU demand.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge is a burstable compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, paired with 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 1 Gbps network baseline. No local storage is bundled, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk capacity, and no GPU hardware is included. Benchmark results show average multi-threaded performance in PassMark and stress-ng, balanced against modest single-core throughput in Geekbench and compression tasks. Memory bandwidth reaches 484.8 GB/sec for small cached reads, supporting up to 7.37 million Redis SET operations per second. The burstable CPU allocation profile offers budget efficiency for workloads with intermittent utilization, making the instance suitable for code compilation, test environments, lightweight web servers, and variable batch processing.
